meaning: Carcharhinus, from Greek karcharias “a kind of shark” (from karcharos “saw-like, jagged”, for its teeth) + rhinus, an ancient word for sharks; albimarginatus, from Latin albus “white” + marginatus “bordered”, referring to its white fin tips
description: A robust grey shark with a bronze sheen, a long broad snout, large round eyes and a ridge between the two dorsal fins. The first dorsal, pectoral and tail fins are all tipped and edged in bright white. It patrols reef drop-offs and offshore banks of the tropical Indian and Pacific oceans, eating mostly bony fish, with rays, small sharks and squid.
eats: Bony fish, eagle rays, small sharks, squid and octopus
